PullRequest.Title: Fix Copilot Sessions Provider to Resolve Changes Summary Correctly
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request addresses an issue with the Copilot sessions provider where it incorrectly attempted to resolve a synthetic file change represented by `summary://changes`. This was causing errors in the latest Insiders session logs.

### Changes Made
- Updated the `copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts` to:
  - Expose aggregate metadata through the existing `ISession.changesSummary` observable.
  - Ensure that the `changes` array remains empty when no actual file URIs are provided.
  - Propagate `changesSummary` correctly through both grouped and single-chat sessions.
  - Update summary values atomically when the underlying session changes.
  
- Added a regression test in `copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts` to validate the fix.

### Validation
- The client transpilation succeeded.
- All tests in the Copilot sessions provider suite passed (83 passing).
- Only the intended files were modified.

This fix resolves the error logged in the Insiders session and improves the handling of session change summaries. Other unrelated performance warnings were noted but not addressed in this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial Copilot background/cloud session inventory and later model-wide refreshes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider construction or an agent-session model change synchronously walks the existing session collection and creates/updates adapters before session change notifications propagate. The added summary extraction and equality check are on this path but are constant-size in-memory work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: All background/cloud sessions in the model are revisited per model change; only sessions carrying aggregate change objects perform the three-field summary allocation/comparison.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh is synchronous and serialized on the model event. The diff adds no tasks, promises, queueing, or concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold sessions create one summary observable. Warm refreshes use structural equality, so unchanged three-field summaries do not notify observers; grouped ISession wrappers remain cached and merely reference the primary chat observable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor, update transaction, cache loop, and equality semantics were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not establish a typical retained-session count or model-event rate, but the incremental work is a bounded three-field object extraction/equality operation amid an already full-session refresh.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds only constant-size state per adapter and coalesces unchanged values; it does not introduce an expensive boundary or materially amplify the existing O(session count) refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering session rows and active-session changes pills when aggregate counts arrive or change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The adapter transaction publishes the summary, then existing autoruns synchronously read it to rebuild a visible row's details or compute the active changes pill. A real summary change can trigger one render/update just as the prior synthetic changes-array update did.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One three-number summary per changed session; session-row rendering is limited to rendered elements, while the existing stats-cache autorun scans visible sessions on dependency changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable updates are transaction-batched and UI reactions run synchronously after the transaction; no new asynchronous fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged summaries are suppressed by structural equality. The existing changes-stats cache is bounded to 30 sessions and authoritative provider summaries bypass aggregation of per-file lists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: adapter transaction, session wrappers, list autorun, and stats-cache reader were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact visible row count and update frequency vary, but the before/after dependency propagation is equivalent: aggregate changes previously changed the synthetic `changes` observable and now change `changesSummary`.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change replaces a synthetic one-element changes array with a constant-time summary read and does not increase render cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or observing session changesets for local and cloud sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changeset observables may lazily resolve checkpoint diffs when consumers observe them. The new summary property is independent of those resolvers, and summary-aware consumers can return before aggregating changesets.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the local Git repository and compute a diff with stats between checkpoint refs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing lazy resolution per observed changeset/ref recomputation; unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local resolver and changeset construction existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks population of that changeset's file list, but not publication or display of the new aggregate summary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch changed files for a GitHub pull request between checkpoint refs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing lazy resolution per observed cloud changeset/ref recomputation; unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same GitHub changed-files request path existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks population of the cloud changeset's file list, but the summary can be displayed without waiting for it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing resolver work scales with observed enabled changesets and changed files, not with the new three-field summary or number of summary updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each existing derived changeset creates an ObservablePromise for its ref pair when recomputed; the diff neither adds resolver invocations nor changes scheduling/concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ObservablePromise/derived state retains the current resolution while observed. The new summary uses adapter-level structural coalescing; no new negative cache or resolver cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changeset construction and both resolver implementations were traced, and the changed summary is only forwarded alongside unchanged changesets.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual resolver frequency depends on which changesets are observed and checkpoint churn, but no changed line adds or increases these calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No filesystem, subprocess, IPC, or network boundary is introduced or moved onto a hotter path; summary consumers may instead avoid per-file aggregation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff hunks. The patch replaces a synthetic file-change object with a structurally coalesced, constant-size aggregate observable and forwards it through cached session wrappers. UI, lifecycle, cache, local-git, and GitHub changeset paths show no introduced performance regression, and there is insufficient evidence to classify the correctness fix as a shipped performance-regression fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
